title: SR-1.24 No CLI command writes vault state beside a live daemon
request: Closes G89: with the daemon stopped five CLI commands wrote vault files (token issue to .memev/tokens.json, project set and backup set to .memev/config.json, devices rename to .memev/devices.json and .memev/jobs.json, bus rename edits bus/ from the CLI process after starting a daemon), measured by hashing every vault file before and after; DESIGN.md says the daemon is the only writer. SR-1.01 closes the log-writing case (claims); this contract closes the state files. Found by the memev twin on 30 October 2026 at main be457db (a sealed run in the twin's evidence). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-1.01, QL-1.02. Sensitive path (the oplog): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge. Also closes issue #248: POST /v1/bus-operator was gated only by the x-memev-client request header (src/server/http.mjs:271, :303), so any loopback token could set the bus operator.

tasks.title: State writes go through the daemon or the lock
requirements: token issue, project set, backup set, devices rename and bus rename make their change through the daemon when it is present (see the presence requirement) and under the SR-1.01 vault lock only when it is not; while the daemon is present none of them writes a vault file from the CLI process
DESIGN.md's one-writer sentence names the state files it covers

every daemon route the CLI uses for a state write, and the existing /v1/bus-operator, requires a local request with the admin scope, the gate /v1/reload uses; the x-memev-client header grants nothing, and bus.resolve gives operator authority to no caller because of it

the CLI calls those routes with the admin token from .memev/admin.json, read without writing; clientToken(root, 'cli') is not used on these paths, so a missing, expired or revoked cli token is never reissued from the CLI

one helper runs every CLI state write: when the daemon is present it sends {op, args} to one local admin route and the daemon runs the same engine function; when it is not, the helper runs that function under the SR-1.01 vault lock and reads the files inside the lock

the daemon is present when .memev/daemon.lock or .memev/daemon.json names a live pid, or a live process holds the SR-1.01 vault lock; then the CLI routes through the daemon, waiting up to 10 s for /healthz, or exits non-zero naming the pid; it takes the offline path only when none of these holds
a refused, failed or timed-out daemon call ends the command non-zero with a message; the CLI never retries and never falls back to a direct write

a config change made through the daemon merges only the changed keys into config.json as it is on disk at that moment and then reloads the daemon's copy; the project pin is the realpath of the CLI's git top-level folder, computed in the CLI and sent with the request

read commands (devices list, license status, status) never write from the CLI process: registry setup (hostDevice, ensureHost, migrate) runs in the daemon when it is present and under the SR-1.01 lock when it is not
token issue sends the requested scopes, paths, ttl and remote flag, and the daemon stores exactly those
backup set validates the URL with assertBackupRemote and changes origin in .git/config and backup.remote in config.json together, in the daemon; a refusal changes neither
